residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been a resident of Maine for at least 6 months before filing; or the parties were married in Maine and one party still resides there; or the grounds for divorce arose in Maine. (19-A M.R.S. §901)

waitingPeriod.description: No judgment of divorce may be entered until at least 60 days after service of the summons and complaint on the defendant. (19-A M.R.S. §902)

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Marital Differences
noFault.description: There exist irreconcilable marital differences between the parties

fault.name: Utter Desertion for Three Years
fault.description: Utter desertion continued for 3 consecutive years prior to the filing of the complaint

fault.name: Gross and Confirmed Habits of Intoxication
fault.description: Gross and confirmed habits of intoxication from the use of liquor or drugs

fault.name: Nonsupport
fault.description: Nonsupport when the spouse has sufficient ability to provide and grossly or cruelly refuses or neglects to provide suitable maintenance

fault.name: Mental Illness
fault.description: Mental illness requiring confinement in a mental institution for at least 7 consecutive years prior to filing

groundsForDissolution.notes: Maine has both no-fault and fault-based grounds. The most common ground is irreconcilable marital differences (no-fault). Fault grounds include adultery, impotence, extreme cruelty, 3-year utter desertion, intoxication, nonsupport, cruel and abusive treatment, and 7-year mental illness confinement. (19-A M.R.S. §902)

propertyDivision.description: Maine courts divide marital property equitably, considering the contribution of each spouse to the acquisition of marital property (including homemaking), the value of each spouse's non-marital property, the economic circumstances of each party, and the length of the marriage.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Non-marital property includes property acquired before the marriage, acquired by gift or inheritance, acquired after a judicial separation, and property excluded by agreement. Non-marital property is generally not subject to division.

legalCitations.description: Jurisdiction and residency — 6 months or married in Maine or grounds arose in Maine
Grounds for divorce — irreconcilable marital differences; 60-day waiting period from service
Division of marital property — equitable distribution
Spousal support — general, transitional, reimbursement, and nominal
Parental rights and responsibilities (Maine's term for custody)
Maine Child Support Guidelines — income shares model

filingFees.notes: Maine filing fees are approximately $120 for a divorce complaint. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Financial Statement (Family Matter)
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, expenses, assets, and debts (Maine Rule of Civil Procedure 108)

basic.name: Judgment of Divorce
basic.description: Final court judgment dissolving the marriage

service.name: Personal Service
service.description: Service by sheriff or other authorized person

service.name: Acceptance of Service
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Proposed Order on Parental Rights and Responsibilities
withChildren.description: Required proposal for allocation of parental rights and responsibilities and parent-child contact

withChildren.name: Child Support Affidavit
withChildren.description: Financial disclosure for child support calculation per Maine Child Support Guidelines (19-A M.R.S. §2001)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Maine Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Maine must file an answer within 20 days of service (additional time may be granted)

responseDeadlines.statute: Maine Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 12(a)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Maine uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Maine Child Support Guidelines table based on combined gross income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Maine recognizes four types of spousal support: (1) General support — based on financial needs and the other party's ability to pay; (2) Transitional support — for a limited period to assist with transition to financial independence; (3) Reimbursement support — for contributions to the other party's education or career advancement; (4) Nominal support — preserving the right to seek future support.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Either party may request spousal support. The court considers the length of the marriage, the ability of each party to pay, the age of the parties, the employment history and earning capacity of each party, the standard of living during the marriage, and the contributions of either party as homemaker.

court.name: District Court, Family Division
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the District Court, Family Division, for the division where either party resides. (4 M.R.S. §152)
